Hello everyone and thank you for participating in the nomination process for the GamerGate Investigatory Commission. The Commission is a project I am running and funding on my own to help create an accurate and detailed timeline and articles about the GamerGate movement/controversy. There will be three "pro-GamerGate," three anti-GamerGate and three neutral panelists on the Commission. The Commission will be voted upon by participants from both pro and anti-GamerGate.

I've received a lot of enthusiasm about this project and also a lot of skepticism. The chief concern people have brought up is that a few third-party trolls volunteered to run as neutrals. Since there is no leader of GamerGate, I put the decision as to whether or not to allow them to volunteer themselves as candidates. The vote was close, but ultimately a majority (57%) of the community voted against allowing trolls to run and their names have been removed from the "neutral" slate.

Another concern that was raised was the potential for vote manipulation. Unfortunately this means that votes used being made through Tor and other proxies will be discarded, so please do not use Tor when voting. If you have any additional concerns, I encourage you to voice them here or contact me about them.

The voting process will begin in approximately two days and run for a period of twenty-four hours, giving everyone an opportunity to participate, regardless of time zone. The voting information and link will be shared on /r/KotakuInAction, /r/AgainstGamerGate, /v/KotakuInAction, /v/GamerGate, GamerGate HQ, GamerGate Revolt, GamerGate.community, /v/ and other GamerGate discussion hubs.

Right now I am waiting for a few of the undecided nominees to make their decision. I am also giving everyone the opportunity to write a one-paragraph campaign statement explaining who they and why they would be good for the Commission. Campaign statements are optional. All undecided nominees must get back to me with a response by 12:00 PM Wednesday (noon 9/2/2015), Central Standard Time.

Obsidian Entertainment Say Linux's Future Is Good With Pillars Of Eternity

I just played about 8 hours last night, and I gotta say there are few games that run as well on linux as PoE. It actually runs better than on Windows 8.1 on the exact same hardware, which I can't say about anything else I own except for Unturned - and that could be due to recent massive updates (the creator is out of college for the summer).

I truly hope Obsidian stay dedicated to Linux.

I'll be blunt: I hated on this game pretty hard when I learned early on that they had no intention of supporting multiplayer. Tack on Obsidian, which I'm sure we've all had one or two bad experiences with, and it was just something I wanted to stay well away from.

That said, if they're making a serious effort to support gaming on Linux, I may throw money at them just to support the cause. I've really been holding out for Sword Coast Legends in this genre given the above concerns, but we need as much exposure as we can get.

And to any development houses out there in the same spot as Obsidian (RE: "We basically had to build our Linux infrastructure from scratch on our side. It wasn't something we were used to."), just put the word out to the community. We want Linux gaming to take off, and there are tons of us out here with years of administration experience that are willing to get you started pro bono, if it means getting the ball rolling.
